headline: INSTAGRAM RAISED ITS VIDEO CEILING FROM 20 MINUTES TO 90, PUT IT ON APPLE TV, AND SAID IT IS TOO EARLY TO TALK ABOUT PAYING FOR IT
deck: Instagram briefed press yesterday on Features, horizontal video up to 90 minutes, with up to eight Reels that link back to the full thing.  Adam Mosseri has spent years saying he did not want long-form on Instagram.  The part nobody is leading with is the money, because there is not any — Meta says it is too early to talk about how creators get paid for it.  Which tells you exactly who is expected to fund long-form video on Instagram.
tldr: Instagram raised its video ceiling from 20 minutes to 90, put it on Apple TV, gave creators up to eight Reels that link back to the full video, and said it is too early to discuss how anyone gets paid for it, against YouTube's 55 percent revenue share.  Price long-form Instagram work as brand-funded production rather than as media, and write the eight linking clips into the contract as named deliverables because on that platform the clip is the distribution.

iSpot found streaming video converted at 3.49 percent against linear television's 0.69 percent, and that 15 of the same 30 brands still recorded more total conversions on linear while a streaming impression costs roughly 3.4 times more.  Ask every video seller for conversions per thousand dollars alongside conversion rate, and calculate it yourself from spend and conversions if they will not give it to you.

Glossy's survey of 90 brand and retailer professionals found creator hauls and unboxing videos fell 14 points in planned use and were the only tactic to decline in both planned use and rated past performance, while streaming advertising went from 23 percent to 45 percent.  Rewrite your next creator brief so the video answers a question or runs a test instead of opening a box.

Resemble AI flagged 8.9 percent of 37,768 advertising files on Meta as generated or manipulated, found brands making selfie-style testimonials that imitate real customer footage, and counted two of 3,379 flagged files disclosing it.  Put a named, clickable human in front of your next testimonial-style advertisement and turn on content credentials in your editing software this quarter.

InStyle has done more than 107 million views across 15 seasons and 87 episodes of a comedy series shot on an iPhone in its own office with its own staff as the cast, and its parent company is now copying the format across other titles.  Cast two or three recurring people before you settle the format on your next owned series, and commit to eight to twelve episodes on a fixed day before spending anything on a guest.

YouTube published its own microdrama figures — 6.5 billion views in the first half of the year, watch time up more than 50 percent, and 40 percent of views arriving more than 30 days after upload.  Move final measurement on vertical serial integrations to 90 days, and make the product do a legible job inside one 60-second scene so a viewer arriving two months late still sees it.

A mobile esports final in the Philippines peaked at 1.49 million, down 11.8 percent, posted its second-best average audience ever at 178,700, and missed the hours-watched record because the show ran shorter.  Contract average concurrent viewers as the measure on every live sponsorship, and when a seller quotes hours watched, ask for total airtime and divide it yourself.
